messages:
customer_acme_inc: Hey team — our rerank endpoint started returning 400s around 10:07am UTC. Error from our client: "400 Bad Request: request validation failed: 'candidates' must be a non-empty array".

customer_acme_inc: Minimal request we sent (redacted):
```json
{
  "request_id": "req-789",
  "queries": ["best laptop for developers"],
  "candidates": []
}
```

sam_support: Thanks for the report — sorry about the interruption. Two quick Qs: 1) did you change client version recently? 2) can you share the full response body (not just client UI message)?

customer_acme_inc: We just updated the search filter last night. Full response: "{\"error\":\"validation_error\",\"message\":\"candidates array must contain at least one candidate\"}". We can repro locally by filtering out all results (so candidates becomes empty).

sam_support: Got it. Our rerank API requires at least one candidate per request (it's in the docs but easy to miss). Two options: 1) have client skip calling rerank when there are zero candidates, or 2) send a single fallback candidate placeholder. Which would you prefer?

customer_acme_inc: Ideally the client should skip the rerank call. But we want the server to return a clearer error so we can triage faster. Right now our logger just shows 400 and we can't tell source.

nik_ml: FYI from model side — the rerank model expects candidate metadata and scores arrays aligned with queries. Empty candidates is an invalid shape, we currently validate in the API layer and return 400. I can add a more descriptive error message from the service: e.g. "400 Bad Request: candidates must be a non-empty array of candidate objects".

maria_sre: If we change the message we should log a migration-safe message and avoid breaking clients that parse error strings. Suggest adding an explicit error_code field (e.g., "ERR_RERANK_EMPTY_CANDIDATES") and keep message human-friendly. That'll help support and customers.

sam_support: Sounds good. Customer, repro steps we recommend so you can patch client quickly: in your frontend where you build candidates, add guard like:
```js
if (!candidates || candidates.length === 0) {
  // skip rerank call
  return candidates;
}
```
Or fallback payload to rerank: send one dummy candidate with minimal fields, e.g.
```json
{
  "id": "fallback-1",
  "text": "No results",
  "metadata": {}
}
```

customer_acme_inc: Ok we'll add guard. Can you provide the curl we used to reproduce so our QA can run it?

nik_ml: Repro curl below — this will return 400 since candidates is empty:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"request_id":"repro-123","queries":["x"],"candidates":[]}'
```

maria_sre: I'll file a quick follow-up to add an error_code and slightly clearer message. @deploy-bot can you queue a tiny change on the validation layer (non-breaking) to include error_code?

deploy-bot: queued change: add ERR_RERANK_EMPTY_CANDIDATES code and update message. pipeline: small validation tweak, unit tests added. ETA ~2 days. :truck: :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam_support: Thanks all. customer_acme_inc, please reply here after you push the client guard so we can close. Also if you want, we can add a server-side soft-fallback (count as feature request) but would prefer clients explicitly skip calls for efficiency.

customer_acme_inc: Will do. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
